newsitem.title: YUGOSLAVIA: Three wounded in Kosovo attack on Serbian police.
newsitem.headline: Three wounded in Kosovo attack on Serbian police.

text.p: Two policemen were seriously wounded in Serbia's troubled province of Kosovo when their vehicle was attacked on Monday, the Yugoslav news agency Tanjug reported.
It said the policemen came under automatic weapons fire on a road in the Srbica area of Kosovo. A passenger in the vehicle was slightly wounded.

The agency said two "terrorist attacks" on police had occurred in the province over the last two days. In the other attack, a police vehicle was shot at and damaged on a road near the village of Bradas.
The attacks coincide with court proceedings against 21 ethnic Albanians last week. They are charged with belonging to a "hostile terrorist association".
No trial date has been set.
The group was charged with a number of premeditated murders and attempted murders in several dozen attacks on policemen, police stations, refugee buildings and other locations.
Kosovo, where ethnic Albanians outnumber Serbs nine to one, is widely regarded as a political powder keg which, if ignited, could wreck international peace efforts in the Balkans.
Some 30 people, both Serbs and Albanians, have been killed over the past year in guerrilla violence.
Serbian police cracked down in the province in January, arresting some 70 people in a sweep after the guerrilla wave.

The United States has made an improvement in Serbia's treatment of Kosovo one of its conditions for lifting remaining sanctions in force against federal Yugoslavia, made up of Serbia and the tiny republic of Montenegro.

Serbia revoked Kosovo's autonomy in 1989, claiming its Albanian population wanted to secede and join neighbouring Albania. Albanians have boycotted Serbian institutions since then but they have been warned by the United States that secession is not an option.
